primitives.verbatim_quote: (Continued) Primary Examiner — Charles T Shedrick (74) Attorney, Agent, or Firm — Bookoff McAndrews, PLLC (57) ABSTRACT Examples disclosed herein may generate a refined and denoised body pose data from a video feed of a sporting event.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\hat{P}': 'Refined body pose data (dimensionless skeleton configuration)', 'V': 'Video feed (spatiotemporal broadcast)', 'L': 'Location data (player coordinates)', 'f_{\\theta}': 'Denoising and refinement function parameterized by learned model'}
primitives.assumptions: Assumes accurate initial tracking data, sufficient temporal resolution, and geometric consistency between player locations and skeletal configurations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degradation occurs when tracking fails to associate correct locations with body parts, leading to incorrect pose hypotheses.

primitives.name: Correspondence Selection
primitives.verbatim_quote: Tracking data containing player locations may be used to determine correspondence between a location and a body pose.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p^*': 'Selected body pose hypothesis (dimensionless skeleton)', 'P': 'Set of all possible body pose hypotheses', 'l': 'Player location (Cartesian coordinates)', 'd(\\cdot, \\cdot)': 'Distance metric (Euclidean or geodesic)', '\\arg\\min': 'Operator returning argument that minimizes the function'}
primitives.assumptions: Assumes each location corresponds to exactly one body part, and the search space over poses is finite and well-defined.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when multiple poses have identical minimal distances, creating ambiguity in selection.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Feature association in multi-target tracking; GSE - Action recognition via spatiotemporal linking.
layer2.telemetry: Pose selection accuracy, false positive rate in ambiguous scenarios.

primitives.name: Length Ratio Estimation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The body pose data may be refined to estimate the length of missing limbs or limbs with unusual length ratios.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L_i^{refined}': 'Estimated length of limb i after refinement (meters)', 'L_i^{raw}': 'Raw limb length from pose data (meters)', '\\alpha_i(\\mathbf{x})': 'Scaling factor dependent on observed limb configuration \\mathbf{x}', '\\mathbf{x}': 'Vector of known limb lengths and joint angles'}
primitives.assumptions: Assumes anthropometric priors hold, limb proportions follow statistical distributions, and the scaling function is learnable from training data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Inaccurate estimates arise when the athlete's physical characteristics deviate significantly from the assumed distribution.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Dimensional calibration of tracked points; GSE - Kinematic chain validation through geometric constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Relative error in estimated limb lengths, improvement in closed-loop kinematic consistency.

primitives.name: Outlier Filtering
primitives.verbatim_quote: The body pose data may further be fltered to filter out unwanted body poses such as body poses of spectators or noisy body poses.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\Pi': 'Set of filtered body poses (dimensionless skeletons)', 'P': 'Original set of body pose hypotheses', 'g(p, S)': 'Discriminant function measuring compatibility of pose p with scene context S', '\\tau': 'Threshold hyperparameter (unitless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Assumes valid poses lie within a low-density region of invalid configurations, and the discriminant captures relevant geometric and contextual cues.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Filtering failures happen when legitimate rare poses are incorrectly classified as outliers, or noise masquerades as valid structure.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Background subtraction and object classification; GSE - Anomaly detection in player trajectories.
layer2.telemetry: Precision-recall trade-off, false rejection rate of genuine player poses.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is reconstructing a coherent skeletal configuration from sparse, noisy, and potentially inconsistent measurements. This is framed as an inverse problem where the forward model maps latent body poses to observable player locations. The denoising step leverages geometric priors and anthropometric statistics to regularize the solution space. Outlier filtering acts as a posterior check, discarding hypotheses that violate spatial coherence with the scene. The correspondence selection bridges the gap between high-level tracking and low-level geometry, ensuring that each location is linked to the correct anatomical site. These operators form a cascaded inference pipeline: first, establish tentative associations; second, refine these associations using internal consistency; third, prune implausible configurations. Failure modes typically involve violations of geometric closure (e.g., limb lengths not summing correctly) or contextual plausibility (e.g., a pose suggesting a player is standing upside-down).
